caveats: Mouse hallmark gene sets use MGI gene symbols — confirm the DE table's gene symbols match this convention (case-sensitive Title Case for mouse) before joining, or remap if needed

With only 12000 genes profiled (likely a filtered/curated set, not the full ~20-25k mouse protein-coding genome), hallmark set coverage may be partial — report the fraction of each hallmark set's genes actually present in the measured background
steps.question: Which MSigDB hallmark pathways are enriched among genes changing between HFD and chow in mouse liver, using both the significant DE gene set (ORA) and the full DESeq2-ranked gene list (GSEA)?
acceptance_criteria: Uses the MSigDB mouse hallmark gene sets (MGI gene symbols, ~50 sets) staged in this environment as the pathway reference; if absent at run time, reports that hallmark enrichment could not be performed rather than substituting a human gene set
Runs GSEA (fgsea) on the full DESeq2 ranked list (e.g., ranked by sign(log2FC)*-log10(pvalue) or the Wald statistic) against hallmark sets, reporting NES and padj per pathway
Runs a threshold-based ORA on the significant DE gene set (padj<0.05, |log2FC|>1) against the same hallmark sets as a complementary check, reporting odds ratio/padj per pathway
Outputs a combined table of hallmark pathways with GSEA NES/padj and ORA odds-ratio/padj, sorted by GSEA significance
Flags any hallmark pathway result driven by fewer than 5 leading-edge genes as low-confidence

plan.title: Mouse liver HFD vs chow: DE genes + hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq raw gene-level counts (Salmon, mouse gene symbols) for 12 mouse liver samples: 6 high-fat diet (treated) vs 6 chow (control), unpaired, single batch. The data profile flags sample_01 with library size ~4x below median, which threatens size-factor estimation and DE power/false positives if left unaddressed — this is handled explicitly as a QC step before modeling rather than silently accepted or silently dropped. Step 1 performs QC on raw counts (library size distribution, PCA/sample correlation) to characterize sample_01's severity and decide (with documented, pre-specified criteria) whether it is retained with a note, downweighted, or excluded, and re-runs the DE model both with and without it if borderline, so the caveat is investigated rather than just repeated. Step 2 runs standard negative-binomial differential expression (DESeq2) for treated vs control on raw counts, with the QC decision from step 1 applied. Step 3 takes the ranked/significant gene list from DE and runs pathway enrichment against the MSigDB mouse hallmark gene sets (the organism-matched hallmark collection staged in this environment, MGI symbols) via both a threshold-based (ORA on significant DE genes) and rank-based (GSEA/fgsea on the full ranked gene list) approach, since GSEA is more robust for a hallmark-collection query with 12k measured genes and moderate n=6/6. Outputs: a DE gene table (log2FC, padj) flagging sample_01 handling, and a hallmark pathway enrichment table with NES/padj, directly answering which genes and which hallmark pathways differ between HFD and chow liver.
